summary: This manuscript resolves four foundational structural, dynamical, stability, and optimization open questions in intermediate-rank (1 < r < d) double-bracket flows (DBFs) for simultaneous multi-excited-state preparation. Specifically, it establishes: (1) exact block-isospectral invariance and graph support connectivity criteria generalizing overlap conditions along with complete hyperbolic Morse index classification; (2) exact cross-subspace dissipation identities and concentration-ratio sharpening guaranteeing dissipation up to r*gamma_min; (3) exact 2-level discretized period-2 stall bifurcations, product-formula complex spectra, and unbalanced-mode Chebyshev instability thresholds; and (4) subset-optimal degenerate weight dualities and adaptive untracked-gap asymmetry rules. The analytical results are backed by an extensive machine-checked Lean 4 formalization (20 theorems, zero sorry, zero Classical.choice), an AST-audited exact-rational Python verification pipeline with 16 SHA-256 certificates, and 60 adversarial tests.
strengths: Comprehensive resolution of four major open analytical problems left by recent concurrent literature (Aghaei Saem et al., arXiv:2611.34871v1).
Unprecedented verification rigor combining rigorous continuous-time analysis with 20 constructive Lean 4 theorems and 16 exact-rational SHA-256 cryptographic certificates.
Brings profound mathematical clarity to quantum algorithm design by identifying exact stability boundaries, stall orbits, and optimal weight configurations.
weaknesses: The exposition is exceptionally dense, requiring deep familiarity with matrix differential equations, algebraic topology (flag manifolds), and Lean 4 formalization.
Some practical quantum implementations remain constrained by hardware noise and state-preparation overheads, though theoretical convergence guarantees are now firmly established.
